greeting.text: Oh. Sam. Hi. It's Judy. From the office. Yes, I work here now. Don't make the face.

options.sam: Hi Judy. Good to see you. I'd like to purchase a ticket.

judy.text: Good to see you too. A ticket. Yes. That's what I do now. I sell the tickets. It's a transition period, Sam, people have those.

options.sam: Judy! From the office! Wow. One ticket, please.

judy.text: Don't 'wow' me. I know how it looks. I ran a department, and now I'm in a glass box with a lanyard. It's very temporary. One ticket. Fine.

options.sam: I finished the spreadsheet, actually. Can I get a ticket?

judy.text: You did not finish the spreadsheet. I checked after you left. And please don't tell anyone from the office you saw me here. A ticket.

core.text: So the way it works now, and I'm only explaining this because you're staring, is I've got the little machine. You tap it, it prints, I tear along the dotted line, except the dotted line is more of a suggestion since they changed paper vendors. The old vendor was a family business, lovely people, the daughter went to dental school. The new vendor is just a website. You can't call a website, Sam. I tried. I was on hold with a website for forty minutes, and my manager, who is nineteen, came over and asked if I needed help. With a phone. I managed a budget of four million dollars. Anyway. That's the machine. It's over here. I'll get to it.

judy.text: I'm getting to it. Patience, Sam. I've got all day. That's the thing about this job. I've got all day.

options.sam: I'm so sorry about the website. Could I get a ticket?

judy.text: Thank you, that's kind. Don't be kind, it makes it worse. Nobody says sorry anymore. Except in China.

options.sam: The manager who is nineteen, yes. Is the ticket in the machine?

judy.text: The ticket is in the machine, yes. Tyler. His name is Tyler. The machine was made in China, actually, it says so on the bottom.

core.text: Which, I went to China. Last spring. By myself, which people made a thing of. That's where the money went, if you're wondering why I'm here. It was worth it, I'm not apologizing. Beijing, then Xi'an, then a boat. We saw the Wall. It's long. People say that, and then you see it, and you think, no, it's really long, they weren't exaggerating. Our guide was a young man named Kevin, which I don't think was his real name, and he said, Judy, you walk faster than anyone in this group, and I said, Kevin, I ran a department. Sam was in it. I didn't tell Kevin about the theater. I got altitude sickness on a bus, which I didn't know you could do.

options.sam: That sounds amazing. One ticket, when you get a chance.

judy.text: It was amazing. You should go. Not now, you have a movie. And you never used your vacation days, I had to sign off on all of that. I had sign-off, Sam. I had a stamp.

options.sam: Altitude sickness on a bus. Right. Ticket?

judy.text: On a bus, Sam. Kevin had to pull over. The whole group watched. It was still more dignified than this booth. You'd have brought me a water.

options.sam: Kevin sounds great. I would also love a ticket, like Kevin would want.

judy.text: Kevin would not want that. Kevin wanted everyone back on the bus by four. He reminded me of you, before the spreadsheet. He'd be mortified to see me in this box.

core.text: Anyway. The thing about the Wall is you can't see the end of it from where you're standing. You just have to go. That's not a question. I'm just telling you that. And this, the booth, the lanyard, Tyler, this is not the end of the wall either. Beijing is nine hours ahead or thirteen behind, depending on how you want to feel about it.

final.text: All right. Here's a ticket. Second row, on the aisle, it has your name on it. It's good to see you, Sam. Really. Don't tell anyone. And Sam. The spreadsheet.

pa.text: Sam, if you can hear this, the popcorn is not complimentary. Tyler made me say that. Enjoy the film.
